note.headline: QQQ falls further below its 200-day average; SPY nears its 1-month low

summary.thesis: Tech (QQQ) is in a downtrend and slipped further below its 200-day average. The broad market (SPY) still holds its long-term trend but is now 0.9% above its 1-month low. Fear is normal, but only 25% of stocks are above their 50-day average. The selling is wide, not panicked.
summary.decision: Stand aside for both long-term buying and swing trades.
summary.act_at: A QQQ close above 681.41 (its 200-day average) ends the tech downtrend and would support a selective stance. An SPY close below 733.00, then 729.58, would point to a deeper decline.

note.happening: On Nov 16, SPY closed at 739.95, down 1.91% from 754.37. QQQ closed at 661.75, down 2.67% from 679.89. Over the past 20 trading days, SPY is down 3.46% and QQQ is down 7.88%. Both are below the past year's highest closes, which came on Oct 6: 779.09 for SPY and 759.66 for QQQ. The DATA classes QQQ as a downtrend because it is below both its 50-day (716.59) and 200-day (681.41) averages. It classes SPY as sideways because it is below its 50-day (763.52) but above its 200-day (729.58). The latest stored VIX reading is 19.3 from Nov 13, up from 18.7. The Nov 16 reading isn't stored yet. DATA reports no news since the last note.
note.business: Taken together, the readings show a broad, orderly pullback led by tech. Trend: tech's long and short trends are both down. The broad market's long trend holds, but its short trend is broken. Fear: the VIX is 19.3, inside the 'normal' 15–20 band, though it ranks at 75 against the past 252 readings. That is near the top of normal, not yet 'elevated'. Weak breadth with only normal fear suggests investors are trimming steadily rather than panicking. That leaves room for more downside before a washout, but it is not a crisis signal either.

worth.text: This is a market note, so no fair value is estimated. The levels below are price-trend markers, not valuations.
worth.key_assumption: No valuation is implied. The levels are price-trend markers only.

bull: SPY is still 1.4% above its 200-day average of 729.58, so the broad market's long-term trend counts as up.
Fear is in the 'normal' band at 19.3, as of Nov 13. The selling has not turned into panic.
Both indices are still above the Nov 5 lows (QQQ 647.05, SPY 733.00), so the recent lows are holding for now.
bear: QQQ is 3.0% below its 200-day average of 681.41 and 8.3% below its 50-day of 716.59. The tech trend is down on both measures.
Breadth fell to 25% of stocks above their 50-day average. Weakness is spread across the market, not just in a few names.
SPY is only 0.9% above its 1-month low of 733.00. A close below it would set a new 1-month low, and its 200-day average of 729.58 sits just under that.

levels.what: QQQ 200-day average. Per the market gate, a close above it ends the tech downtrend. That would support a selective stance.
QQQ 50-day average. A close above it would put tech's short-term trend back up and pass the pipeline's market check. That would be the cue to lean in more.
QQQ 1-month high (Oct 28). A close above it would mean the tech pullback is fully recovered.
SPY 50-day average. A close above it would put SPY's short-term trend back up.
SPY 1-month high (Oct 21). A close above it would mean SPY's pullback is fully recovered.
SPY 1-month low (Nov 5). A close below it would set a new 1-month low, meaning the decline is continuing.
SPY 200-day average. A close below it would put the broad market's long-term trend down too.
QQQ 1-month low (Nov 5). A close below it would mean the tech decline is continuing.

longterm.why: The last note stood aside after QQQ closed below its 200-day average. Since then QQQ has fallen further, from 679.89 to 661.75, and breadth has slipped from 27% to 25%. SPY's long trend and normal fear suggest the damage is contained for now. Still, the readings don't support new buying until QQQ closes back above 681.41.

swing.why: QQQ closed at 661.75, 8.3% below its 50-day average of 716.59. Per the trend gates, setups keep failing the pipeline's market check until QQQ closes above that level.

decision.timing: NVDA reports earnings after the close on Nov 17 (estimated date). Per DATA, it carries big index weight, so its report moves the whole tech group. It lands with QQQ 2.2% above its 1-month low and 3.0% below its 200-day gate. change_mind: A QQQ close above 681.41, its 200-day average, would end the tech downtrend per the market gate and move the stance toward selective. A close above 716.59 would pass the pipeline's market check.

A SPY close below 733.00 (1-month low), and especially below 729.58 (200-day average), would put the broad market's long-term trend down too and strengthen the case to stay aside. A QQQ close below 647.05 would confirm the tech decline is continuing.

note.headline: Tesla slips below a key zone as margins and cash flow keep shrinking

summary.thesis: Tesla's sales have stalled, and its margins and cash flow are falling, but the stock is still priced near the top of its own 5-year valuation range and far above every cash-flow value.
summary.decision: Long-term: avoid. Swing: no trade while the price sits between support at 364.02–368.6 and resistance at 380.15–389.95.
summary.act_at: Revisit long-term near 293.94; no swing trade until a close above 389.95 or below 364.02

note.happening: Tesla closed at 379.74, down 2.69% on the day. That puts it just under the 380.15–389.95 zone, the price area that buyers and sellers have fought over most (10 touches). Tesla opened Cybercab pre-orders for personal use with a $299 monthly fee, and a €3B Berlin Gigafactory expansion for the Cybercab was reported. The next earnings report is on 2027-01-27.
note.business: The numbers that change the business are getting worse. Revenue in the latest quarter was down 0.17% from a year earlier, after growing 15.78% two quarters ago. Operating margin, the share of each sales dollar left after running costs, fell to 3.35% from 4.74%. Trailing free cash flow, the cash left after spending, fell to 3.3B from 6.8B. The filings show inventory up 15% while quarterly sales were up 0%, which can force price cuts. Each dollar invested now earns 5¢ a year, against 33¢ three years ago. Some things are not at risk. Tesla holds 37.5B of net cash, so funding the €3B Berlin expansion (reported) is not a solvency question. The Cybercab pre-orders and Mercedes-Benz's new city driving assist (reported) matter for the self-driving story and competition, but neither shows up in revenue yet. The Tesla–SpaceX merger talk is speculative and is a governance and sentiment story, not a business one.

worth.text: At 379.74, Tesla is valued at a market cap of 1501.0B. That is 14.5 times sales and 417.9 times trailing earnings. The data says this price needs about 52% a year growth, while Tesla delivered 3% a year over 3 years. A cash-flow model (DCF) that discounts future free cash flow at about 10% gives 20.09 / 24.79 / 44.69 per share across bear, base and bull. Even with 30% starting growth, it gives only 44.29. If operating margin falls to 1%, the value drops to 21.41. The second method asks what the stock would cost at its usual price-to-sales range over the last 5 years. It gives 203.8 / 293.94 / 399.81, and the current multiple sits at the 77th percentile of that history. The huge gap between the two methods comes from one question: do investors keep paying for future hopes such as autonomy and robotaxis, or do they start paying for today's cash flow? The fair-value range below assumes the first, which makes it the generous view.
worth.key_assumption: The market keeps valuing Tesla within its own 5-year price-to-sales range instead of on current free cash flow.

bull: Net cash of 37.5B gives Tesla room to fund the Cybercab and Berlin plans without stress.
Trailing revenue still rose to 103.6B from 95.6B, and quarterly growth was 15.78% just two quarters ago.
The Cybercab personal-use pre-orders at a $299 monthly fee point to a possible recurring revenue stream beyond car sales.
bear: Operating margin fell to 3.35% from 4.74%, and trailing free cash flow fell to 3.3B from 6.8B.
At 417.9 times trailing earnings, the price needs about 52% a year growth against 3% a year delivered over 3 years.
Inventory rose 15% while quarterly sales rose 0%, which raises the risk of price cuts that squeeze margins further.

levels.what: Today's close. It is near the top of the own-history range and many times every cash-flow value (24.79 base).
The top of the own-history price-to-sales range. Above it, even the generous method calls the stock expensive.
The middle of the own-history range. At this level the stock no longer needs a top-of-range multiple, so it earns a fresh look if margins stop falling.

longterm.why: Sales have stalled while margins and cash flow are falling, and the price still needs a top-of-history multiple. The business is graded D and the rules committee call is Reduce.

swing.why: The trend is a flat range, and all three moving averages (375.25 to 385.94) are flat. The price sits between support at 364.02–368.6 and resistance at 380.15–389.95, and both zones are close compared with the 16.56 average daily move, so a stop would sit inside normal noise. A close above 389.95 or below 364.02 would show a direction.

decision.timing: Options price a 14.7% move by the 2027-01-15 expiry, before the 2027-01-27 report. That report is the next real test of margins and cash flow, and the Cybercab and merger headlines do not change that timing.

change_mind: The 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin back above 4.74% and quarterly revenue growth heading back toward the 15.78% of two quarters ago.
The price falls to around 293.94, the middle of the own-history range, while operating margin holds at 3.35% or better.
Trailing free cash flow recovers from 3.3B back toward 6.8B, which would narrow the gap to the cash-flow values.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still avoid. The close at 379.74 broke below the 380.15–389.95 zone, which confirmed that buyers are not defending the stock near the top of its valuation range.
note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: NVIDIA falls 4.12% to 156.14 before tomorrow's report; hold, no trade

summary.thesis: NVIDIA is a grade A business, and at 156.14 its price assumes slower cash-flow growth than its recent results show, but the stock is falling, has no support level below it, and reports earnings tomorrow.
summary.decision: Long-term: hold. Swing: no trade until after the 2026-11-17 report.
summary.act_at: Hold at 156.14; add near 151.37 only after a clean report; trim near 224.74

note.happening: NVDA fell 4.12% to 156.14. It is in a downtrend, below its 20-day (195.64), 50-day (213.15) and 200-day (203.75) averages, and no support zone sits below the price. NVIDIA reports earnings on 2026-11-17. On 2026-11-16 the company announced the Rubin HPC GPU and the expanded Vera CPU platform, and said it swept the MLPerf benchmarks. A TechCrunch headline reported Sam Altman discussing 'Nvidia without Jensen Huang', which keeps the reported leadership questions in the news.
note.business: Things that change the business: in the latest reported quarter, sales grew 105.85% from a year earlier, up from 73.21% two quarters before. Operating margin rose to 65.21% from 58.09%. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) was 127.0B over the last year, up from 72.0B. Cash and liquidity are not a worry: net cash is 23.2B. Two things in the filings are at risk. First, margin is at the top of its 5-year range of 16–65%. Second, unpaid customer bills grew 127% while quarterly sales grew 106%, so some sales may have been pulled forward or customers may be paying more slowly. Things that change sentiment or governance: today's product news (Rubin HPC, Vera, quantum work) comes from company announcements, not filings, and gives no revenue figures, so it supports the long-term story without changing near-term numbers. The reported CEO questions and $946.6M of insider sales outside pre-set plans are governance and sentiment issues. They do not show up in demand or cash today. Segment data is not available, so data alone cannot tell us which product lines drive growth.

worth.text: At 156.14, the market is pricing free cash flow to start growing about 20.8% a year and then slow down. A discounted cash-flow model (today's value of future cash, at a 10.1% discount rate) gives 151.37 at 20% starting growth and 220.46 at 30%. The model's base case is 224.74, with a bear case of 193.13 and a bull case of 267.17. Valued on its own past price-to-sales levels, the stock comes out at 217.35–411.04, because the current price-to-sales of 12.4 sits at only the 9.0th percentile of its own 5-year range. It is also below the peer median of 16.6. The earnings multiple is 19.7 on trailing results and 9.9 on next year's estimates. The gap between methods comes down to one assumption: growth. Analysts expect 70% EPS growth next year, but the model caps starting growth at 30%. Margin is the other big lever. If operating margin falls to 48%, value drops to 113.77. At 32%, it drops to 76.17. My range is 151.37–224.74.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow starts growing 20–30% a year and operating margin stays near today's 65.21% instead of fading toward 48%.

bull: Quarterly sales growth sped up to 105.85% from 73.21% two quarters ago, and margin rose to 65.21%.
Next-year earnings estimates rose 23.7% over 90 days, which puts the stock at 9.9 times next year's EPS.
Price-to-sales of 12.4 is below the peer median of 16.6 and at the 9.0th percentile of its own 5-year range.
bear: Operating margin of 65% sits at the top of its 5-year range, and value drops to 113.77 if margin falls to 48%.
Unpaid customer bills grew 127% while quarterly sales grew 106%, a sign that sales may have been pulled forward.
The price is in a downtrend below the 50-day average of 213.15, with no support zone below 156.14 and insider sales of $946.6M outside pre-set plans.

levels.what: Today's close. It implies about 20.8% starting cash-flow growth, which the business has beaten recently. That is a reason to keep holding, but not to add the day before the report.
Value at 20% starting growth, the low end of the range. Add here only if the 2026-11-17 report shows operating margin near 65.21% and customer bills growing in line with sales.
Base-case cash-flow value. Near this price most of the valuation upside is used up, so reassess and consider trimming.

longterm.why: The automated rule says 'Buy now' and the business is grade A, but the committee says 'Hold', and the technical, macro and risk views are all negative. The value case supports owning the stock. The report tomorrow and the receivables warning argue against adding before the numbers are out.

swing.why: There is no support level below the price to place a stop under, and resistance sits just above at 163.9–169.14. Options price a 10.3% move by 2026-11-20, more than the 9.84 average daily range (ATR), so the report can gap past any stop.

decision.timing: No action before the 2026-11-17 report. Implied volatility of 81.0 against realized volatility of 53.9 (1.5x) shows the market expects a big move. After the report, compare revenue with the 108.7B estimate and EPS with the 2.47 estimate, and check margin and customer bills before acting at 151.37 or 224.74.

change_mind: Add instead of hold: the report beats the 108.7B revenue estimate, operating margin holds near 65.21%, and the price stays at or above 151.37.
Turn cautious or trim: operating margin falls back toward the prior 58.09%, or customer bills again grow much faster than sales (127% against 106% last time).
Swing entry: a daily close back above the 169.14 top of the first resistance zone after the report, which would end the run of lower highs.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still hold and no swing trade; the 4.12% drop to 156.14 brought the price nearer the 151.37 add level, but with no support below it and the report due on 2026-11-17, it is still too early to add.
note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: AMD drops 5.58% to 504.28, nears support; still above every fair value

summary.thesis: The business is growing faster and earning more, but at 504.28 the price already assumes far more growth than any valuation method in the data supports.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait. Swing: wait, because the price is between a support zone and resistance less than one typical daily move away.
summary.act_at: Long-term buy case starts at 333.38. Swing only on a hold of 480.33–502.6 and a close above 530.13.

note.happening: AMD fell 5.58% to 504.28. It is now below the 517.35–530.13 zone, which acted as support last time and is now overhead resistance. The price sits just above the next support zone at 480.33–502.6, which has been tested 5 times. There is no new news, and the next earnings report is on 2027-02-02.
note.business: The business itself did not change today. Only the mood around the stock did. The latest filing, from 2026-11-04, is strong. Sales grew 44.68% from a year earlier, faster than the 37.85% two quarters ago. Operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) rose to 17.72% from 8.78%. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) grew to 7.1B from 5.4B. The company has more cash than debt, with net cash of 8.7B, so its finances are not at risk. Analysts keep raising their numbers: next year's EPS (earnings per share) estimate rose 12.1% in 30 days to 17.69. Two risks are real. First, inventory rose 57% while sales rose 45%, which means unsold product is building up and could force price cuts that hurt margins. Second, the 17.72% operating margin is near the top of AMD's 5-year range, and peaks like this usually fade. Separately, insiders sold $12.8M outside pre-set plans. That is a governance and sentiment signal, not a change to the business.

worth.text: Every method in the data puts fair value well below the price. A cash-flow model (DCF: today's value of future cash) gives 146.48 in the bear case, 187.98 in the base case and 222.62 in the bull case. AMD's own price-to-sales history gives 179.24 to 333.38. Today the stock trades at 18.2 times sales. That compares with a peer median of 13.7 and sits at the 92nd percentile of AMD's own 5-year range. On earnings it trades at 109.9 times trailing EPS but 28.5 times next year's estimate. That gap shows the price leans on next year's earnings showing up. The main reason the methods disagree with the price is the growth assumption. The models cap starting cash-flow growth at 30%, which gives 184.49. The price implies starting free-cash-flow growth of 59.2%. If operating margin fell to 13%, value would drop to 97.39.
worth.key_assumption: Starting free-cash-flow growth: the price implies 59.2%, while the models cap it at 30%, which yields 184.49.

bull: Sales growth is speeding up: 44.68% last quarter versus 37.85% two quarters ago.
Operating margin roughly doubled, to 17.72% from 8.78%, and free cash flow rose to 7.1B from 5.4B.
Analysts raised next-year EPS by 12.1% in 30 days to 17.69, which puts the forward P/E (price divided by expected earnings) at 28.5.
bear: At 504.28, the price is above the top of the fair-value range, 333.38. The base DCF is 187.98.
Inventory is up 57% against sales up 45%, a setup that can lead to price cuts and lower margins.
Price-to-sales of 18.2 is above the peer median of 13.7 and at the 92nd percentile of AMD's own 5-year range.

levels.what: Today's close. It is above every valuation method, so it is not a buy price.
Bottom of the 480.33–502.6 support zone, tested 5 times. A close below it would mean the trading range is breaking down. Even then, the price would still be above fair value.
Top of the fair-value range, the high end of AMD's own price-to-sales history. The valuation case for buying starts here.

longterm.why: The business is improving fast, but the price needs 59.2% starting cash-flow growth to make sense. The highest fair value in the data is 333.38.

swing.why: The trend is a range. The 20-day average of 517.33 is falling, and the price is below the 50-day average of 555.09. Resistance at 517.35 is less than one ATR (average daily range) of 41.28 away, so the upside does not cover the risk. A setup would be the price holding 480.33–502.6 and then closing above 530.13. If 480.33 breaks, the next support is 451.0–469.22.

decision.timing: Earnings on 2027-02-02 are not close yet. However, options priced off 534.06 imply a 16.3% move by 2026-12-18 and 20.4% by 2027-01-15, and recent actual volatility (124.4) is running above implied volatility (75.2), so large swings like today's can continue before the report.

change_mind: A close below 480.33 would break the range and put the 451.0–469.22 zone in play. That would end any swing setup, though the long-term call would still be wait.
A drop to 333.38 or lower, the top of fair value, would turn the long-term call from wait toward buy, provided the operating margin holds near 17.72%.
If the next filing shows inventory still growing faster than sales (now 57% vs 45%), or the next-year EPS estimate falls back below 15.78, the call would move toward avoid.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait, because today's 5.58% drop to 504.28 still leaves the price far above the 333.38 top of fair value; the low end of the range moved slightly, to 146.48 from 148.51.
note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: Amazon falls 3.3% to support; cash burn keeps us waiting

summary.thesis: Margins are improving, but slowing sales, deep cash burn and a price near the top of its value range leave little room for error.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for a lower price. Swing: no trade while the price is stuck between support and resistance.
summary.act_at: Wait. Consider buying at 251.93 only if cash flow improves; fuller value is at 238.65.

note.happening: Amazon closed at 257.75, down 3.34% on the day. That puts it just above its main support zone of 251.93–257.04 and just below resistance at 258.08–261.12. The biggest reported news is a Vulcan rocket failure that destroyed 40 Amazon Leo satellites (speculative). Zoox robotaxis are also now available on Uber in Las Vegas. No earnings date is in the data.
note.business: Three things in the latest filing (2026-10-30) affect the business itself. First, sales growth is slowing. Quarterly revenue rose 12.09% from a year earlier, compared with 16.61% two quarters ago. Second, profitability is improving. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, rose to 13.09% from 11.02%. Third, cash is going the wrong way. Free cash flow, the cash left after spending on the business, is -46.9B over 12 months, against +10.6B a year earlier. Debt exceeds cash by 66.7B, though liquidity of 114.2B leaves no near-term funding strain. The filings also flag that unpaid customer bills are up 61% while sales are up 12%, which can mean sales were pulled forward. The reported satellite loss hurts the Leo internet project and its timeline, but not Amazon's core demand. The Zoox, Instagram affiliate-link and James Bond reports affect sentiment and long-term options, not this year's numbers. Most at risk: cash flow, and whether today's peak margin holds. Not at risk: overall scale, with revenue of 797.5B over 12 months.

worth.text: No discounted-cash-flow value is available because free cash flow is negative. Value rests on Amazon's own price-to-sales history (price compared with yearly sales per share). That method gives 187.93 at the low end, 238.65 in the middle and 266.4 at the top. At 257.75, the price sits in the upper part of that range. Price-to-sales of 3.5 is at the 82nd percentile of Amazon's own 5-year history. The filing risks note that the price needs about 34% a year growth, against 13% a year delivered over 3 years. Against peers, Amazon looks cheap: their median price-to-sales is 6.8, and the growth-adjusted ratio versus peers is 0.6. The gap between the two methods comes down to one question: is Amazon valued like its own history or like its peers? Earnings multiples point the same cautious way. The price is 20.9 times trailing earnings but 24.2 times next year's, because analysts expect next-year EPS (10.67) to be below this year's (12.8). Note that the valuation summary in DATA quotes a stale price of 266.66.
worth.key_assumption: Amazon's price-to-sales stays within its own 5-year range and does not move toward the peer median of 6.8.

bull: Operating margin rose to 13.09% from 11.02%, so each dollar of sales now earns more.
Price-to-sales of 3.5 is about half the peer median of 6.8, with growth-adjusted EV/sales at 0.6 of peers.
Next-year EPS estimates rose 1.4% over 30 days, and revenue grew to 797.5B from 691.3B over 12 months.
bear: Free cash flow fell to -46.9B from +10.6B a year earlier, and debt exceeds cash by 66.7B.
Quarterly sales growth slowed to 12.09% from 16.61% two quarters ago, while unpaid customer bills rose 61%.
Next-quarter EPS estimates were cut 2.6% in 30 days, and next-year EPS of 10.67 is below this year's 12.8.

levels.what: Bottom of the strongest support zone (6 touches). A first entry only if free cash flow stops getting worse.
Bottom of the deeper support zone (9 touches), near the 200-day average of 244.69. A close below it breaks the range.
Middle of the own-history value range, where price and fair value meet.

longterm.why: Better margins do not yet outweigh slowing growth and cash burn at a price in the upper part of the value range. The business grade is D and the committee call is 'Reduce'.

swing.why: The price sits in a narrow gap between support at 251.93–257.04 and resistance at 258.08–261.12, so the upside to resistance is small for a sensible stop. Recent swings (realized volatility 40.1) are also bigger than options price in (implied volatility 33.2).

decision.timing: No earnings date is in the data. Options to 2026-11-20 price a move of about 3.9%, so the next point to reassess is a test of 251.93 or a close above 261.12.

change_mind: A filing showing 12-month free cash flow back above zero (from -46.9B) while the price holds 251.93 would turn 'wait' into 'buy'.
A close below 244.3, the bottom of the deeper support zone, would shift the stance toward 'avoid' until the price nears 238.65.
A close above 267.56, the top of resistance, would break the range, but it would also put the price above the 266.4 value top. That would not by itself justify buying.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still 'wait', because the 3.34% drop to 257.75 leaves the price above the 238.65 value midpoint while free cash flow stays at -46.9B.
note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: Microsoft slips 1.12% to 517.99 on no news; still a hold

summary.thesis: Microsoft is growing faster and earning wider margins, but free cash flow fell from 78.0B to 60.0B, so the price only holds up if earnings, not today's cash flow, set the value.
summary.decision: Hold for the long term and add only near strong support. No swing trade from the middle of the range.

note.happening: The stock fell 1.12% to 517.99, with no new headlines since the last note. That puts it just under the 50-day average of 519.36 and above the first support zone at 504.96–512.76. The next report is on 2027-01-27, and analysts have raised their next-year EPS estimate to 24.2, up 2.2% in 30 days.
note.business: The business itself keeps improving. Revenue grew 18.8% from a year earlier in the latest quarter, up from 18.3% two quarters ago. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, rose to 47.1% from 46.27%. The weak spot is cash. Free cash flow, the cash left after spending on equipment and data centers, fell to 60.0B from 78.0B over the trailing year. That puts the free-cash-flow margin at only 17.31%. The filings note that each dollar invested now earns 30¢ a year against 51¢ three years ago, so the heavy spending is not paying back yet. The balance sheet is not at risk: net cash is 29.0B and liquidity is 64.5B. Today's 1.12% drop came with no news, so it moves sentiment only. The new risk headings in the annual report are a disclosure matter, not a change in demand. What is at risk is the payback on the spending. Demand and margins are not at risk today.

worth.text: The methods disagree sharply. A cash-flow model built on today's 60.0B of free cash flow gives a base value of 220.42 (bear 182.25, bull 291.45). bear: Growth is slowing: quarterly sales growth fell to 11.85% from 16.19% two quarters ago.
Estimates keep falling: this quarter's earnings-per-share estimate was cut 7.3% in 30 days, to 0.68.
The margin is at a 5-year peak of 31%. A fade to 23% would put value at 58.22, below today's 60.75.

levels.what: Low end of the own-history price-to-sales range, next to the 60 put strike with the most open interest (38265). This is where to start a first, small position.
Value if operating margin fades to 23%. Buying here means the margin-peak risk is already paid for, so this is where to add.
DCF base value. Above it the margin of safety is gone, so no buying there.

longterm.why: The business is grade B and cheap on most measures. But the old floor broke, no support appears below the price, and estimates are still being cut. The plan is to buy lower, at prices that already allow for some margin fade.

swing.why: The trend is down: lower highs and lower lows, below the falling 20-, 50- and 200-day averages (63.88, 68.83, 80.38), and no support level is listed below 60.75. There is no trade until the stock closes above the 20-day average of 63.88 and the 64.56–65.08 resistance.

decision.timing: The 2027-01-19 report comes after the 2027-01-15 option expiry, and options price a move of about 11.7% by that date. With estimates still falling, any buying before the report should stay small and stay at 60.37 or below.

change_mind: A close above 65.08, the top of resistance, with the price back above the 20-day average of 63.88, would end the downtrend case and reopen a swing entry.
If the next-quarter earnings-per-share estimate climbs back from 0.92 to its 30-day-ago level of 0.94, the cuts have stopped, and buying could start nearer 60.75.

If the 2027-01-19 report shows quarterly sales growth below 11.85% together with operating margin falling from 31.3%, the fair-value range moves toward its 52.3 low and the 58.22 add level would be too high.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait, but the first buy level moves down from 61.63 to 60.37 because the stock closed at 60.75, below the old support zone that now shows as resistance at 61.14–61.64.
note.label: Research, not advice.
